subject.title: Feat: Add Trivy SBOM and vulnerability scanning to Docker release

question: After the checkout regression and scanner-scope defect are fixed, should Docker releases immediately fail on fixed CRITICAL Trivy vulnerabilities, or should Trivy start as advisory-only SBOM/SARIF reporting?
rationale: The PR adds a production release dependency, Code Scanning writes, and a release-failing security policy that static checks cannot validate and that may intentionally block Docker releases.

options.title: Fix, prove, then gate
options.body: Restore current-checkout verification, scope the gate to the intended vulnerability policy, require redacted live workflow output and artifacts, then let release/security owners decide the blocking gate.

options.title: Start advisory-only
options.body: Land SBOM/SARIF/artifact generation without the release-failing exit path until maintainers observe successful release runs.

options.title: Accept blocking risk
options.body: A release/security owner can intentionally accept the external scanner dependency and own Docker release failures after merge.

recommendation.title: Fix, prove, then gate
recommendation.body: Restore current-checkout verification, scope the gate to the intended vulnerability policy, require redacted live workflow output and artifacts, then let release/security owners decide the blocking gate.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Docker release, release-control, and security history make this the strongest routing signal for the backfill and release-gate decision.
